title: Tenant-aware spill grouping and miniblock compactor to reduce KV cache fragmentation
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Under mixed tenant workloads we observed increased spillback churn and fragmentation in the KV cache when tenants with dissimilar allocation patterns interleaved. This caused frequent small spills and high tail latency for eviction-sensitive requests. Goal: reduce cross-tenant fragmentation and spill volume while keeping eviction latency bounded and avoiding tenant starvation.

What this PR does: Implements two complementary subsystems: 1) tenant-aware spill grouping: when the pager decides to spill pages, it now prefers to aggregate spill candidates by tenant and miniblock locality so we emit larger contiguous spill objects that are easier to rehydrate and compress, and reduce write amplification to storage. 2) miniblock compactor: a lightweight in-memory compaction pass that runs opportunistically on recently freed miniblocks (cache-aligned micro-pages) to coalesce adjacent free miniblocks into larger reusable extents that match kernel-friendly allocation sizes. The compactor runs in the background with an adaptive backoff based on CPU pressure and scheduled priority relative to request batching.

Design highlights: - Tenant buckets: pages/proto-extents are annotated with tenant_id and hotness score. The spill scheduler groups candidates by tenant_id and preferred device segment; grouping reduces cross-tenant interference and enables better per-tenant QoS. - Miniblock units: we introduce a 4KB-aligned miniblock descriptor layer to track contiguous free runs inside segments; compaction attempts to merge miniblocks into 64KB and 256KB extents depending on workload heuristics. - Priority-aware evictor: eviction selection now factors in fragmentation penalty and spill-grouping impact; the evictor will defer evicting small highly-fragmented segments that are likely to be resolved by the compactor, preferring cold, low-fragmentation targets first. - Kernel alignment: compactor emits extents aligned to the runtime's optimized kernel tiling sizes so subsequent token-generation kernels avoid inefficient kernels due to unaligned pages.

Implementation notes: - New modules: kv/miniblock_compactor.{cc,h}, kv/spill_group_scheduler.{cc,h} and scheduler hooks in kv/evictor.{cc}. - Metrics: added kv.compactor.run_count, kv.compactor.coalesced_bytes, kv.spill.group_size_histogram, kv.eviction.fragmentation_penalty. Dashboards updated in observability-pack. - Config knobs: compactor.enabled (default true), compactor.cpu_limit_pct, spill.group_minimum_bytes (default 64KB), eviction.fragmentation_threshold. These are runtime-configurable via the console flags and can be tuned per-deployment.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for miniblock merging logic and tenant grouping heuristics. - Integration harness: synthetic tenants with skewed object-size distributions and churn validated that spill count dropped and spill write throughput became more sequential. - Perf lab: ran the benchmark-lab suite with a 50/30/20 (hot/warm/cold) tenant mix over 24h. Observed 28% reduction in total bytes spilled, 34% drop in small spill events (<16KB), and 12% improvement in P99 request eviction latency under load. See perf_summary for numbers.

Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag. Start with dev and perf clusters, Canary on dedicated pools for one week, then enabled in Hosted for low-traffic customers and finally global rollout. The compactor runs at a low default CPU cap and self-throttles to avoid interference.

Rollback and safety: feature flag allows immediate disable. Compactor is idempotent (it only merges free miniblocks) and the grouping logic does not change on-disk object format. We add extra telemetry to detect evictor starvation and spill staging regressions.

Related work: complements previous spill-smoothing and eviction scheduler improvements; this PR focuses on reducing fragmentation at a miniblock granularity and grouping spills for better downstream IO profiles.

Notes: The description intentionally keeps the spill output format compatible with existing restore logic; no on-disk layout migration required.

ci_checks:
Initial CI run: build OK, unit tests OK, integration timed out on long-run harness. Reran with split tests: all checks passed (build, unit, smoke-integration, lint). Perf-nightly scheduled.
Checks: build/linux: pass, lint: pass, unit: pass, integration-smoke: pass, integration-nightly: scheduled, coverage: pass
perf_summary: Perf lab (50/30/20 tenant mix) over 24h: total_spill_bytes -28%, small_spill_events(<16KB) -34%, P99 eviction latency -12% (from 420ms to 371ms), P99 generation tail improved by 7ms on average; CPU overhead of compactor ~2.6% on dedicated test pools when enabled with default limits.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory efficiency: tenant-aware spill grouping and miniblock compaction reduce fragmentation and spill write amplification. Default enabled; can be toggled via compactor.enabled and per-tenant skip flags.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: feature.kv_miniblock_compaction. Default ON for new clusters. Monitor kv.compactor.coalesced_bytes, kv.spill.group_size_histogram, kv.eviction.fragmentation_penalty and runtime CPU usage. If eviction delays appear, disable compactor or reduce compactor.cpu_limit_pct.
validation: Unit tests added for merging logic and grouping. Synthetic integration verified grouping behavior with deterministic tenants. Perf harness benchmark YAML included. No on-disk format changes. Backcompat validated against existing restore code.
risk: Medium: background compaction introduces CPU usage and scheduling interactions. Mitigated by adaptive backoff and CPU cap. Non-breaking to on-disk formats.
followups: 1) ENG-5833: extend grouping to prefer co-located device segments for multi-region deployments. 2) ENG-5901: add cross-tenant QoS controls exposed in Console. 3) Investigate hardware-accelerated compaction in future (ENG-6010).
